Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).
source_name: Maria Axenovich, António Girão, Lawrence Hollom, Julien Portier, Emil Powierski, Michael Savery, Youri Tamitegama and Leo Versteegen, “A note on interval colourings of graphs”, arXiv:2303.04782 (2023).
statement: A graph is **biregular** if it is bipartite and all vertices in the same part have the same degree. A graph is **interval colourable** if it has a proper edge-colouring in which the colours incident with each vertex form an interval. **Hansen's conjecture.** Every biregular graph is interval colourable. The source describes this as a longstanding conjecture and gives no resolution.
title: Hansen's biregular interval-colourability conjecture
